newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA URGED TO HELP SMALL BUSINESSES.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA URGED TO HELP SMALL BUSINESSES.

text.p: The government should spell out concrete measures to stimulate small and medium enterprise (SME) in South Africa in the parliamentary session which starts on Friday, political consultant Lawrence Schlemmer said on Wednesday

Schlemmer, in a review commissioned by the South African Chamber of Business, said President Nelson Mandela's speech opening parliament and Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget speech in March "are awaited with rather anxious anticipation".
"One has a sense that what is required is an action breakthrough of some kind...Obviously this cannot be a short-run and unsustainable fix to stimulate demand," he said.
"It would seem as if the answer has to lie in the additional stimulation of SMEs, which would have the additional benefit of boosting flagging business confidence," Schlemmer said.
Discussing political stability, Schlemmer said an increase in Afrikaner ethnic dissent was inevitable because of a perception that Afrikaans language rights had been downgraded.

"This trend is made additionally serious by the fact that, of all the major non-foreign ethnic categories in South Africa, only Afrikaners no longer have any representation in the central executive of the country.
"This is very dangerous in a country which has a predisposition to ethnic mobilisation," Schlemmer, a former politics lecturer at the University of the Witwatersrand, said.

"A serious question can be posed as to whether the government...has been conscious enough of the dynamite which a loss of ethnic status can ignite in a society with marked ethnic identities," he said.
